title: Heartbeat-checkpoint integration with parallel executor
description:
## Goal

Integrate heartbeat-and-per-SNR-boundary checkpointing with the
parallel executor: SIGINT mid-run flushes a checkpoint with the
per-worker state from design-doc §4 schema v2; `--resume` from that
checkpoint produces byte-identical deterministic columns vs an
uninterrupted reference run at the same seed.

## Context

Task under story `bcf7776d` (CPU foundation) within epic `gf2-sim`
(`f9717e7e`). Phase 0 design doc:
`dev/active/ec530af9-pipeline-design.md` §4 (heartbeat schema v2),
§3 (per-worker seek scheme). Sequencing:
- depends on `3fcb7025` (per-worker dispatch must exist)
- depends on `db9836e4` (channels must exist so heartbeat tests
  exercise the AWGN + Rayleigh paths — adds the edge per audit C5)

## AMENDMENT 2026-06-08 (user-approved): CLEAN-CUT v2-only, NO migration, NO backward compat

Two amendments fold into this body:

1. **v2-only schema** (earlier amendment): the new pipeline is
   v2-only; `CheckpointReader` loads v2 only.
2. **Clean-cut, no migration** (this amendment, user decision
   2026-06-08): there are **no previous runs and no users**, so there
   is **no v1 backward compatibility and no migration tool** at all.
   The earlier `checkpoint_migrate` binary and every v1-migration
   deliverable/criterion/test are **removed**. This supersedes design
   doc §4's "Migration tool" subsection and the epic's Q5 row
   ("one-shot migration tool for v1") — both updated to record the
   clean-cut decision. The v2 checkpoint schema itself is unchanged.

## Deliverables

1. `crates/gf2-sim/src/checkpoint/mod.rs` containing:
   - `pub struct CheckpointWriter` that serialises per-SNR state to
     `<dir>/snr_<NNNN>.json` per design-doc §4 schema v2
     (`worker_states[]` required, `schema_version: 2`, `config_hash`
     blake3 of the serialised `PipelineConfig` excluding the
     path-dependent `checkpoint_dir` / `tracing_log_path` fields).
   - `pub struct CheckpointReader` that loads **v2 only** and restores
     per-worker `rng_word_pos`. A non-v2 `schema_version`, a
     `config_hash` mismatch vs the live config, or an unparseable file
     is a hard load error (`FatalError::BuildError(BuildError::
     ConfigHashMismatch)`). There is no v1 path of any kind.
   - Atomic write: write to `.tmp`, fsync the file, rename, fsync the
     directory — all errors propagated (contractual durability).
2. Integration with the parallel executor (`gf2-sim::parallel`):
   - A serial SNR-sweep runner (`run_sweep_checkpointed`) looping
     `config.esn0_db_points`, loading any existing v2 checkpoint via
     `CheckpointReader` when `--resume`, delegating to the per-SNR
     `run_snr_point_checkpointed` (SNR-boundary flush + heartbeat-
     interval flush via `heartbeat_every_frames`).
   - SIGINT handler installed via `ctrlc`; on signal: stop accepting
     new batches, let in-flight workers settle on a frame boundary
     (CPU drain), flush checkpoint, fsync. The **non-zero process
     exit** lives in the `checkpoint_sweep` driver binary (never in
     library code).
3. Tests in `tests/checkpoint_compat.rs`:
   - v2 round-trip resume: a v2 checkpoint loads and resumes on the
     N-worker path, byte-identical `fer / frames / errors /
     mean_iters` vs an uninterrupted N-worker reference run.
   - Real subprocess 10-SNR SIGINT→`--resume` byte-identity, one
     non-ignored fast-tier test per channel (AWGN, Rayleigh, Rician),
     each guaranteeing the SIGINT lands mid-run.
   - Atomic kill-during-fsync: a writer SIGKILLed while in `fsync`
     leaves either a complete previous-state checkpoint or no new file
     — never a partial JSON.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] SIGINT mid-run on a 10-SNR sweep flushes a v2 checkpoint
  per the design-doc §4 schema; re-invoking with `--resume`
  produces byte-identical `fer / frames / errors / mean_iters`
  vs an uninterrupted reference run at the same seed across all
  three channel types (AWGN, Rayleigh, Rician).
- [hard] Atomic write: a test that kills the writer mid-flush (via
  signal **after the tmp bytes are written and before the atomic
  rename** — amended 2026-06-08 from "during fsync", which cannot be
  instrumented from user space; the durability contract is the
  no-torn-file invariant, not proof of being inside the syscall)
  leaves either a complete previous-state checkpoint or no new file
  at all; never a partial JSON.
- [hard] `cargo-ci`, `code-review` gates green.

## Non-goals

- GPU-pipeline drain semantics (owned by Phase C `571c11c4`).
- Across-SNR parallelism checkpointing (epic non-goal — within-SNR
  parallelism is the contract; cross-SNR parallel was the legacy
  `run_coded_iterative_parallel` path that is not migrated).
- **Any v1 backward compatibility or migration** (clean-cut v2-only;
  no prior runs or users — user decision 2026-06-08). The reader is
  v2-only; there is no `checkpoint_migrate` tool and no v1 test.
